# Java code style
- Constructor injection only; no field `@Autowired`.
- Controllers stay thin: validate input, call one use case (input port), map the result to a DTO.
- Business logic lives in the domain and in use cases; persistence adapters contain queries and mapping only.
- Prefer records for value objects and DTOs; keep classes package-private unless another package needs them.
- Use `Optional` for "may be absent" returns, never for fields or parameters.
- Log with SLF4J placeholders (`log.info("id={}", id)`), never string concatenation, never log secrets or full request bodies.
- Mapping: plain constructors / static factories for simple DTOs; introduce MapStruct only when mapping gets non-trivial.
- Methods over ~40 lines or classes over ~300 lines are a signal to split.
